Radiology procedures accounted for $1,040 in Byron Center Medicaid payments in 2024
Y. T. Acosta
In 2024, Byron Center Medicaid providers submitted $1,040 in claims for the Radiology Procedures category, based on data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database. This amount represents a 129.6% rise from the $453 reported for similar services during 2023.
Medicaid is a government-managed health insurance initiative funded jointly through state and federal contributions. Serving low-income families and individuals, seniors, children and persons with disabilities, the program remains a cornerstone of national health care coverage.
As funding is sourced from public tax revenue, fluctuations in Medicaid billing highlight how health care resources are distributed within communities.
The "Radiology Procedures" category comprises Medicaid-billed services organized by type using established HCPCS and CPT code groupings. Under this analysis, each code falls into a single service group based on shared prefixes and ranges, facilitating accurate comparisons, avoiding duplicate counts, and maintaining reliable long-term comparisons.
Medicaid outlays increased in multiple categories, but Radiology Procedures ranked 10th for total Medicaid spending in Byron Center in 2024.
Statewide in Michigan, Radiology Procedures held the eighth position for total Medicaid payments during 2024.
Between the five years prior to 2024, Byron Center’s Medicaid payments connected to Radiology Procedures grew $1,040, or 0%. Certain years saw accelerated increases, particularly in 2023 and 2022.
Distribution of spending on Radiology Procedures was city-wide but concentrated within a few ZIP codes. For 2024, ZIP code 49315 made up $1,040 in claims, representing 100% of Byron Center's Medicaid billing under this category for the year.
Most Medicaid payments for Radiology Procedures focused on a small selection of billing codes.
Comparing locally, Medicaid reimbursements related to Radiology Procedures in Byron Center jumped 129.6% from 2023 to 2024, while overall Medicaid claims in all categories moved up by 13.7% citywide over the same period.
According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, total state and federal Medicaid expenditures reached approximately $871.7 billion in fiscal year 2023, making up about 18% of all health spending in the U.S.—a substantial leap from roughly $613.5 billion recorded for 2019, prior to the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
This increase, estimated at about 40% over several years, has been driven by growth in enrollment and elevated healthcare usage during and after the pandemic period.
Federal budget laws enacted under the Trump administration have presented major plans for Medicaid spending cuts and program changes. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” introduced in 2025, aims to reduce federal Medicaid expenditures by more than $1 trillion over the coming decade and imposes measures such as work requirements and larger cost sharing, potentially scaling back access and support for some enrollees. These amendments are expected to place more financial responsibility on the states and constrain increases in federal Medicaid funding, even as Medicaid continues serving tens of millions nationwide.
